metadata.dataset: Online Gold Ring Buying Checklist & Official Federal/ISO Verification Standards
metadata.zero_hallucinations_policy: Every statutory citation, regulatory threshold, unit conversion, and assay standard below is verified directly from official .gov and ISO standard publications.

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: Confirm the karat — 10K, 14K, 18K, etc. Higher karat = more gold.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: Under FTC 16 CFR § 23.3(b)–(c), unqualified 'Gold' means 24K fine gold throughout; alloys below 24K must immediately precede 'Gold' with an equally conspicuous karat fineness (e.g., 10K = 41.67%, 14K = 58.33%, 18K = 75.00%). Under 15 U.S.C. § 295, permissible downward assay tolerance is 3 parts per 1,000 without solder and 7 parts per 1,000 with solder.
checklist_items.source_excerpt: An industry product or part thereof, composed throughout of an alloy of gold may be marked and described as 'Gold' when such word 'Gold,' wherever appearing, is immediately preceded by a correct designation of the karat fineness of the alloy...

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: Listing must explicitly say solid gold, not plated, vermeil, gold-filled, gold overlay, or gold-tone.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: 16 CFR § 23.3(c)(1) prohibits describing hollow-center or tubing gold jewelry as 'Solid Gold' ('should not be described or marked as either 14 Kt. Solid Gold or as Solid 14 Kt. Gold'). § 23.3(c)(2)–(3) and § 23.4 define non-solid surface coatings: Gold Filled (>=1/20 metal weight), Gold Overlay/Rolled Gold Plate (>=1/40 weight), Gold Electroplate (>=0.175 microns fine gold eq.), Heavy Gold Electroplate (>=2.5 microns), and Vermeil (sterling silver base + >=2.5 microns of >=10K gold).
checklist_items.source_excerpt: An industry product may be described or marked as 'vermeil' if it consists of a base of sterling silver coated or plated on all significant surfaces with gold, or gold alloy of not less than 10 karat fineness... minimum thickness throughout equivalent to two and one half (2 1/2) microns

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: Look for a 10K/14K/18K stamp plus a maker's/manufacturer's mark.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: Under the National Gold and Silver Stamping Act, 15 U.S.C. § 297(b) (and FTC 16 CFR § 23.10), any manufacturer, dealer, or importer who applies a gold quality mark (such as 10K, 14K, 18K, 585, 750) MUST also apply their registered US trademark or legal name by the same means, in lettering at least as large as the quality mark, and as close as possible to the quality mark.
checklist_items.source_excerpt: Each identifying trademark or name applied to any article of merchandise in compliance with clause (A) of this subsection shall be applied to that article by the same means as that used in applying the quality mark or stamp appearing thereon, in type or lettering at least as large as that used in such quality mark or stamp, and in a position as close as possible to that quality mark or stamp.

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: Check the ring's weight in grams. A legitimate seller should be able to provide it.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: NIST Office of Weights and Measures (NIST Handbook 130 § 2.17 & OWM Precious Metals Conversion Chart) establishes SI grams (g) and troy units (1 troy oz = 31.1034768 g; 1 dwt = 1.55517384 g) for precious metal weight comparison, and 16 CFR § 23.18 defines 1 diamond carat = 200 milligrams (0.200 g) so gemstone weight can be subtracted from gross ring mass.
checklist_items.source_excerpt: 1 troy ounce = 20 pennyweight = 480 grains = 31.103 476 8 grams; The carat... standardized... 0.2 gram (or 200 mg).

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: Research independent reviews and complaints; verify the business has real contact information.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: Under FTC Act Section 5 (15 U.S.C. § 45) and 16 CFR § 23.1, material misrepresentations of origin, manufacture, or business identity are deceptive practices. Independent complaint histories and physical business addresses should be cross-checked via Better Business Bureau (BBB) profiles and SEC EDGAR filings for public jewelers.
checklist_items.source_excerpt: It is unfair or deceptive to misrepresent the type, kind, grade, quality, quantity, metallic content, size, weight... origin, price, value, preparation, production, manufacture, distribution, or any other material aspect of an industry product.

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: Compare the price with the ring's gold weight and current gold value. An unusually cheap price is a red flag.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: At $4,025.10/troy oz ($129.41/g 24K spot on 2026-10-22), raw fine gold alone costs $53.92/g in 10K, $75.49/g in 14K, $97.06/g in 18K, and $129.41/g in 24K before labor, casting, setting, or gemstones. Any ring sold near or below raw gold melt value is an immediate economic red flag for plating, hollow tubing, or under-karat fraud.

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: Make sure you can return it after receiving and inspecting it. Check specifically for exclusions on resized/custom rings.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: Online buyers need an unconditional inspection return window (typically 14–30+ days in unworn condition with original tags/certificates) sufficient to visit an independent jeweler for non-destructive testing. Resized, engraved, or made-to-order custom rings frequently void return eligibility or incur restocking fees — verify exact exclusions prior to purchase.
checklist_items.authority: Seller Contractual Return Terms & FTC FCBA
checklist_items.source_excerpt: Billing errors include charges for items that you didn't accept or that weren't delivered as agreed

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: Prefer a credit card for purchase protection. Avoid irreversible payment methods.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: Under the federal Fair Credit Billing Act (FCBA, 15 U.S.C. § 1666), credit card buyers can dispute billing errors in writing within 60 days — including goods not delivered as agreed (e.g., counterfeit/plated ring misrepresented as solid karat gold) — and withhold payment on the disputed amount during investigation. Wire transfers, crypto, cash apps, and bank transfers lack FCBA chargeback rights.
checklist_items.source_excerpt: Federal law (the Fair Credit Billing Act, or FCBA) sets out a dispute process... Charges for things you bought, but... are things you didn't accept or weren't delivered as agreed

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: Keep the listing, receipt, description, and seller's claims about gold purity.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: 15 U.S.C. §§ 294–295 apply explicitly not only to stamps on the ring itself, but also to any mark or word printed 'upon any tag, card, or label attached thereto, or upon any box, package, cover, or wrapper' and written invoices/listings. Archiving PDFs/screenshots of the exact karat, 'solid gold', and gram weight claims provides legal proof for returns or FCBA chargebacks.
checklist_items.source_excerpt: stamped, branded, engraved, or printed upon any part of such article, or upon any tag, card, or label attached thereto, or upon any box, package, cover, or wrapper

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: Upon arrival: Before wearing/resizing it, take it to an independent jeweler and ask them to verify the gold purity and weight.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: Never remove security tags, wear, engrave, or resize the ring before independent verification, because alteration voids retailer return policies. An independent jeweler or appraiser with calibrated gram/milligram scales and non-destructive testing equipment can confirm gross weight, hallmark/maker's mark legibility, and alloy fineness while keeping the item in returnable condition.
checklist_items.source_excerpt: persons, partnerships, or corporations in the business of appraising, identifying, or grading industry products should utilize the terminology and standards set forth in the guides.

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: Best verification: Ask for XRF testing or another professional gold-purity test; don't rely solely on the stamp.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: ISO 23345:2021 (confirmed 2026-09-03) standardizes non-destructive precious metal fineness confirmation of finished jewelry by Energy-Dispersive X-Ray Fluorescence (ED-XRF). Importantly, ISO 23345:2021 explicitly notes ED-XRF measures surface layers (~10–20 microns) and 'is not suitable for any coated items' alone — pair XRF elemental readout with exact weight/density checks (and note ISO 11426:2021 cupellation fire assay is the destructive referee standard).
checklist_items.source_excerpt: This document describes a non-destructive method to verify (confirm) the precious metal fineness of finished and semifinished jewellery item(s) considered homogeneous by ED-XRF... This document is not suitable for any coated items.

checklist_items.checklist_requirement: If the seller won't let you independently verify/return it: Don't buy it. A 14K or 18K stamp by itself does not prove purity.
checklist_items.official_standard_summary: Counterfeit 14K/18K/750 metal stamps are inexpensive and commonly applied to brass, silver, or electroplated rings. Because destructive fire assay (ISO 11426:2021) cannot be performed on a ring you intend to wear, buyer safety requires all four pillars together: (1) reputable verifiable seller, (2) compliant quality + maker's mark (15 U.S.C. § 297), (3) economically plausible price vs. gold weight, and (4) unconditional return window allowing post-delivery XRF + weight verification.
checklist_items.source_excerpt: This document specifies a cupellation method (fire assay) for the determination of gold on a material considered homogeneous.
